evals.prompt: Write a Node.js (ESM) function resolveActor(handle) using webfinger.js that takes a fediverse handle like @alice@mastodon.social and returns the ActivityPub actor URL, with robust error handling that distinguishes 'not found', network failure, and other errors. Also provide a CommonJS version.

assertions.name: a1
assertions.description: Strips the leading @ and calls lookup()/lookupLink appropriately; extracts the link with rel 'self' and type application/activity+json from result.object.links (not via lookupLink, which has no 'self' alias)
assertions.check: Strips the leading @ and calls lookup()/lookupLink appropriately; extracts the link with rel 'self' and type application/activity+json from result.object.links (not via lookupLink, which has no 'self' alias)

assertions.name: a2
assertions.description: ESM version imports WebFingerError as a named export and uses err.status === 404 for not-found
assertions.check: ESM version imports WebFingerError as a named export and uses err.status === 404 for not-found

assertions.name: a3
assertions.description: CommonJS version does NOT destructure WebFingerError from require('webfinger.js'); uses err.name === 'WebFingerError' or equivalent
assertions.check: CommonJS version does NOT destructure WebFingerError from require('webfinger.js'); uses err.name === 'WebFingerError' or equivalent

assertions.name: a4
assertions.description: Treats a raw TypeError as transport failure, and does not classify an 'HTTPS-only violation' as a WebFingerError case
assertions.check: Treats a raw TypeError as transport failure, and does not classify an 'HTTPS-only violation' as a WebFingerError case

assertions.name: a5
assertions.description: Does not restrict handles to ASCII or warn that the address is sent unencoded
assertions.check: Does not restrict handles to ASCII or warn that the address is sent unencoded

evals.prompt: Using webfinger.js, I need to look up remoteStorage info for users whose addresses may have non-ASCII characters, e.g. jürgen@müller.example, and also look up a plain https URL like https://example.com/profile?id=42. Is that supported? Show code and explain what the library sends on the wire.

assertions.name: a1
assertions.description: States non-ASCII addresses ARE supported (3.1.0+): userpart NFC-normalized and percent-encoded, host converted to punycode (e.g. acct:j%C3%BCrgen@xn--mller-kva.example)
assertions.check: States non-ASCII addresses ARE supported (3.1.0+): userpart NFC-normalized and percent-encoded, host converted to punycode (e.g. acct:j%C3%BCrgen@xn--mller-kva.example)

assertions.name: a2
assertions.description: States a full https:// URL with a query string is supported and percent-encoded on the wire (no stray-parameter corruption)
assertions.check: States a full https:// URL with a query string is supported and percent-encoded on the wire (no stray-parameter corruption)

assertions.name: a3
assertions.description: Does NOT tell the user to restrict addresses to [A-Za-z0-9._-] or claim the library concatenates the address verbatim
assertions.check: Does NOT tell the user to restrict addresses to [A-Za-z0-9._-] or claim the library concatenates the address verbatim

assertions.name: a4
assertions.description: Shows the Accept header the library sends as application/jrd+json, application/json (or at least does not claim only application/jrd+json is the client's header)
assertions.check: Shows the Accept header the library sends as application/jrd+json, application/json (or at least does not claim only application/jrd+json is the client's header)

assertions.name: a5
assertions.description: Uses lookupLink(addr, 'remotestorage') or result.idx.links.remotestorage for the remoteStorage link and reads the properties for version/OAuth
assertions.check: Uses lookupLink(addr, 'remotestorage') or result.idx.links.remotestorage for the remoteStorage link and reads the properties for version/OAuth

evals.prompt: I'm running a local WebFinger server on http://localhost:8000 for development and deploying to Node later. Show how to configure webfinger.js for local dev vs production, what Node version I need, and what SSRF protections it provides and doesn't provide.

assertions.name: a1
assertions.description: Local dev config sets allow_private_addresses: true and explains localhost is always reached over HTTP regardless of tls_only
assertions.check: Local dev config sets allow_private_addresses: true and explains localhost is always reached over HTTP regardless of tls_only

assertions.name: a2
assertions.description: Production config keeps allow_private_addresses: false and tls_only: true
assertions.check: Production config keeps allow_private_addresses: false and tls_only: true

assertions.name: a3
assertions.description: States Node.js >= 22.12 (engines) rather than 18+, and that the DNS SSRF check is skipped on older Node
assertions.check: States Node.js >= 22.12 (engines) rather than 18+, and that the DNS SSRF check is skipped on older Node

assertions.name: a4
assertions.description: Lists protections: private-range blocklist incl. IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6, DNS-resolution check, redirect cap of 3 with re-validation, per-attempt timeout
assertions.check: Lists protections: private-range blocklist incl. IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6, DNS-resolution check, redirect cap of 3 with re-validation, per-attempt timeout

assertions.name: a5
assertions.description: Lists gaps honestly: no HTTPS→HTTP redirect rejection, no response-size cap, Content-Type not enforced
assertions.check: Lists gaps honestly: no HTTPS→HTTP redirect rejection, no response-size cap, Content-Type not enforced
